detail.title: Identify Artificial Intelligence
detail.description: Identify which of the following utilizes artificial intelligence in most cases: a. Computer keyboard; b. Spam caller labeling on your cell phone; c. Talk-to-text on your cell phones; d. Stopwatch; e. Amazon Echo Dot; f. Text suggestions in your email; g. Headphones; h. E-scooters.
detail.understand: DS4A defines AI as computer systems performing tasks that generally require or mimic human intelligence, and ML as the subfield where systems improve at a task by learning from data. Test for each item: does it perform a human-like task (recognising speech, judging spam, predicting text) and does it rely on patterns learned from data? Fixed-rule devices are not AI.

questions.explanation: Converts key presses to characters with fixed rules; it does not learn from data.

questions.prompt: Spam caller labeling on your cell phone
questions.explanation: Learns patterns from call data and user reports to label likely spam callers (classification).
Speech recognition is a learned model (today: deep learning) mapping audio to words.
Counts time with a fixed mechanism; no learning or human-like task.
Voice assistant: speech recognition and language understanding are AI/deep-learning systems.
Predictive text models learn from large text corpora which words are likely next.
Play audio; in most cases they perform no task that mimics human intelligence.
Electric motor and controls follow fixed rules; in most cases no learning from data.

detail.interpretation: Answer: b, c, e and f use AI in most cases. a, d, g and h follow fixed, explicitly programmed rules.
common_mistakes: Treating anything electronic or 'smart-looking' as AI.
Forgetting that 'in most cases' matters: some premium headphones or scooters may include AI features, but the typical device does not.
